canonicalExplanation.summary: A **font stack** lists fonts in order of preference: `font-family: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;`. The browser uses the first one available. Web fonts load over the network, so for a moment they **aren't** available — `font-display: swap` shows text in a fallback immediately, then swaps. Pick fallbacks with similar proportions to limit layout jumps, and consider **self-hosting** fonts so visitors' browsers don't contact third-party font servers.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
On a slow connection, your landing page shows blank space where the headline should be for three seconds — the custom font is still downloading. When it finally arrives, the whole page jumps. A system fallback renders immediately while the chosen web font loads with compatible metrics. In this lesson you'll configure a font stack and explain fallback, loading and privacy trade-offs.

examples.title: Text shows before the web font arrives
examples.situation: A system fallback renders immediately while the chosen web font loads with compatible metrics.
walkthrough: **Stack:** `"Inter", system-ui, …, sans-serif` — the system fallback is available instantly.
**Load:** `font-display: swap` means the browser will render text in the fallback while inter-var.woff2 downloads.
**Compatible metrics:** system-ui has similar proportions, so when Inter swaps in, lines barely shift.
examples.result: Text is readable from the first moment, and the swap causes only a small shift.

examples.title: Seven font files for one page
examples.situation: A page loads regular, italic, medium, semibold, bold, black and light weights of one font plus a second display font — 600 KB of fonts.
walkthrough: Most weights appear only once or not at all.
Every file delays the final text rendering on slow networks.
Fix: keep two weights (or one variable font), drop the unused display font, and self-host WOFF2.
examples.result: Font downloads drop to about 60 KB with no visible loss.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Declaring one custom font guarantees it loads before any text is displayed.
misconceptions.correction: Web fonts download separately and may be slow or fail. Provide a fallback stack ending in a generic family, and use font-display to decide whether text shows in a fallback while the font loads.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening predict, what did the text use when Inter failed?

analogy.example: A font stack is like **ordering food with backups**: "the special if it's ready, otherwise the usual, otherwise anything vegetarian". font-display: swap means you start eating the usual while the special is cooking.
usefulFor: seeing swap as not waiting hungry
limitations: Food doesn't cause layout shift; font swaps can.
Ordering from another restaurant (a font CDN) tells them you're here.

remediation.explanation: Checklist: **stack ends in a generic family? font-display set? only used weights loaded? fallback with similar proportions? self-hosted if privacy matters?**

recap.summary: To configure a font stack, list preferred fonts with system fallbacks and a generic family, load web fonts with @font-face and font-display: swap so text shows immediately, choose compatible-metric fallbacks, load only needed weights, and weigh third-party loading against privacy.
